subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a shared async resource lifecycle/shutdown primitive, and if so should it live in the plugin SDK, gateway/channel lifecycle, agent runtime, or remain as targeted local guards?
rationale: Current main has localized cleanup/drain/generation mechanisms, but a shared primitive would cross public plugin SDK and core runtime boundaries; automation cannot choose that product/API direction safely.

options.title: Design a shared lifecycle primitive
options.body: Define a narrow, backward-compatible shutdown/drain/cancel contract and prove it across representative agent retry, plugin cleanup, and gateway restart paths.

options.title: Keep targeted guards only
options.body: Continue fixing concrete lifecycle races at their owner boundary and close this tracker once maintainers decide a central abstraction is not worth the API surface.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Track retry/tool, channel/plugin cleanup, and outbound replay separately if maintainers want concrete fixes without one global ResourceManager contract.

recommendation.title: Design a shared lifecycle primitive
recommendation.body: Define a narrow, backward-compatible shutdown/drain/cancel contract and prove it across representative agent retry, plugin cleanup, and gateway restart paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans plugin SDK, gateway/channel, and agent runtime owner boundaries where prior history and reviews route many lifecycle choices through this area.
